doc: Studio quality scorecard catalogue. Source of truth for studio/evals/scorecard.py and the Desk Scorecard view. Edit here; then run scorecard.py --write-catalogue to refresh the table in TESTS.md.

status.nodata: source file or data not there yet
status.pending: spot-check or monthly result not recorded yet

suites.name: Radar
suites.question: Is the competitor and client-account feed complete, fresh and correct?

suites.name: Patterns & intel
suites.question: Does the Radar turn posts into patterns, visual tags and questions we can trust?

suites.name: Kits
suites.question: Do the client kits hold complete, sourced, conflict-free facts?

suites.name: Creative output
suites.question: Are the finished pieces good, true, compliant and original?

suites.name: Library & learning
suites.question: Is every decision filed so the next piece learns from it?

suites.name: Pipeline
suites.question: How long, how many runs, how many failures, how much usage?

suites.name: Intake
suites.question: Can the 20 test briefs be produced as asked from the kits on disk?

suites.name: Golden creative set
suites.question: Monthly: how good are concepts for 5 fixed briefs, judged with the critic rubric?

tests.name: Coverage: instagram
tests.measures: Share of active instagram accounts in radar/accounts.json that have at least one post in posts.jsonl dated in the last 30 days
tests.computed: accounts.json active (and discoverable != false) on instagram; posts.jsonl grouped by account; count accounts with a post whose `date` is within 30 days. Business Discovery (official API).
tests.why: Patterns are only as good as the accounts they see; a silent platform hides what competitors are doing there.

tests.name: Coverage: youtube
tests.measures: Share of active youtube accounts in radar/accounts.json that have at least one post in posts.jsonl dated in the last 30 days
tests.computed: accounts.json active (and discoverable != false) on youtube; posts.jsonl grouped by account; count accounts with a post whose `date` is within 30 days. YouTube Data API.
tests.why: Patterns are only as good as the accounts they see; a silent platform hides what competitors are doing there.

tests.name: Coverage: web
tests.measures: Share of active web accounts in radar/accounts.json that have at least one post in posts.jsonl dated in the last 30 days
tests.computed: accounts.json active (and discoverable != false) on web; posts.jsonl grouped by account; count accounts with a post whose `date` is within 30 days. RSS/Atom feeds and robots-allowed pages.
tests.why: Patterns are only as good as the accounts they see; a silent platform hides what competitors are doing there.

tests.name: Coverage: facebook
tests.measures: Share of active facebook accounts in radar/accounts.json that have at least one post in posts.jsonl
tests.computed: accounts.json active (and discoverable != false) on facebook; posts.jsonl grouped by account; count accounts with any post. Manual entries only (no scraping), so the bar is low.
tests.why: Patterns are only as good as the accounts they see; a silent platform hides what competitors are doing there.

tests.name: Coverage: linkedin
tests.measures: Share of active linkedin accounts in radar/accounts.json that have at least one post in posts.jsonl
tests.computed: accounts.json active (and discoverable != false) on linkedin; posts.jsonl grouped by account; count accounts with any post. Manual entries only (no scraping), so the bar is low.
tests.why: Patterns are only as good as the accounts they see; a silent platform hides what competitors are doing there.

tests.name: Coverage: tiktok
tests.measures: Share of active tiktok accounts in radar/accounts.json that have at least one post in posts.jsonl
tests.computed: accounts.json active (and discoverable != false) on tiktok; posts.jsonl grouped by account; count accounts with any post. Manual entries and landscape notes only (no scraping).
tests.why: Patterns are only as good as the accounts they see; a silent platform hides what competitors are doing there.

tests.name: Freshness < 48 h
tests.measures: Share of active, fetchable accounts (Instagram, YouTube, web; discoverable) whose newest post was collected (`seen`) in the last 48 hours
tests.computed: max(`seen`) per account in posts.jsonl vs now.
tests.why: Stale data means the nightly ideas react to last week. An expired token shows up here first.

tests.name: Source health
tests.measures: Share of Radar sources (instagram, youtube, rss, manual) reporting ok in radar/status.json
tests.computed: status.json sources[*].ok; error text goes into detail.
tests.why: A dead source silently shrinks coverage; this names it the same night.

tests.name: Metric accuracy (YouTube re-fetch)
tests.measures: Share of 10 random YouTube API posts whose stored views are within 5% of a fresh YouTube Data API read
tests.computed: Seeded random sample (seed = date) of posts with source youtube-api, preferring ones seen in the last 48 h; videos.list?part=statistics with YOUTUBE_API_KEY from studio/.env (never printed); |stored - fresh| / fresh <= 5%. 1 quota unit. Skipped with --offline.
tests.why: Outlier multiples drive what we copy; wrong view counts mean we chase the wrong posts.

tests.name: Duplicate rate
tests.measures: Share of posts that duplicate another (same id, same normalised URL or video/shortcode, or same account + caption + day)
tests.computed: posts.jsonl; URLs normalised (YouTube watch/shorts/youtu.be -> video id, Instagram /p/ /reel/ -> shortcode, else host+path).
tests.why: Duplicates inflate counts and pattern hits.

tests.name: Date sanity (no fetch-time dates)
tests.measures: Posts whose `date` looks like the collection time or is impossible
tests.computed: Count posts with a timestamped date within 2 minutes of `seen`, a date-only date equal to the `seen` day on non-API sources, a date more than 1 day after `seen`, a date before 2005, or 5+ posts of one account sharing one exact timestamp.
tests.why: A fetch-time date makes an old post look new and breaks the 30-day windows and outliers.

tests.name: Posts with a real date
tests.measures: Share of posts that carry their own date
tests.computed: posts.jsonl `date` not null.
tests.why: Undated posts can't enter windows, outliers or patterns.

tests.name: Hours since last Radar run
tests.measures: Age of radar/summary.json lastRun
tests.computed: now - summary.lastRun.
tests.why: The nightly job must actually run.

tests.name: Patterns with real support
tests.measures: Number of patterns in radar/patterns.json with 3+ example posts from 2+ different accounts
tests.computed: patterns[*].examples looked up in posts.jsonl for their account.
tests.why: Fewer than 3 examples from one account is an anecdote, not a pattern.

tests.name: Share of patterns that are supported
tests.measures: Share of listed patterns meeting the 3-examples / 2-accounts bar
tests.computed: as above / len(patterns).
tests.why: Unsupported patterns should never reach the strategist.

tests.name: Pattern precision (spot-check)
tests.measures: Share of sampled pattern examples that truly show the pattern's mechanism
tests.computed: Orchestrator opens 2 examples from each of 5 random patterns (10 posts), looks at the thumbnail/caption and marks match / no match. Written to reviews/<date>.json as {test:'intel.pattern_precision', value:%, sample:[post ids], verdict, notes}.
tests.why: Keyword rules mislabel posts; this is the only check that a pattern means what it says.

tests.name: Client-fit specificity
tests.measures: Average share of all kits that a pattern's clientFit lists
tests.computed: mean(len(clientFit) / number of kits) over patterns.
tests.why: A pattern that 'fits' every client tells the strategist nothing.

tests.name: Visual tags on top posts
tests.measures: Share of the 50 highest-outlier competitor posts of the last 30 days that have visual tags in radar/visual.json
tests.computed: Top 50 by outlierRaw (competitor accounts only, dated in 30 days); ids found in visual.json (any of: {posts:{id:..}}, {id:..}, [{id|post|postId}], {items:[..]}).
tests.why: Formats and hooks are half the story; the look is what the director needs.

tests.name: Question-mining yield
tests.measures: Number of audience questions in radar/questions.json
tests.computed: len(questions) (list, {questions:[..]} or {items:[..]}).
tests.why: Real questions are the cheapest source of hooks that land.

tests.name: Question de-dup
tests.measures: Share of mined questions that are unique after normalisation
tests.computed: Lowercase, strip punctuation; duplicates = exact normalised match or token Jaccard >= 0.8.
tests.why: Duplicate questions crowd out new ones and fake a trend.

tests.name: Candidate accounts awaiting a decision
tests.measures: Accounts proposed in radar/candidates.json that nobody has accepted or rejected yet
tests.computed: Items without status accepted/rejected/added/approved/dismissed.
tests.why: Unreviewed candidates mean coverage gaps stay open.

tests.name: Client accounts mirrored
tests.measures: Share of kits whose own Instagram posts are in radar/clients.json (so new pieces avoid repeating them)
tests.computed: clients.json clients[*].posts > 0 / number of kits.
tests.why: The strategist can only avoid repeats it can see.

tests.name: Average completeness
tests.measures: Mean kit completeness (12 key fields) across kits/_index.json
tests.computed: mean(completeness) x 100.
tests.why: Every empty field is a TODO in a piece or a proof-only post.

tests.name: Provenance coverage
tests.measures: Share of filled key fields that name a source in kit.json provenance
tests.computed: Key fields: name, city, province, group, brokerage.name, brokerage.licence, agent.licence, photo, footer, logos, colors.accent (not 'default'), complianceLine.
tests.why: An unsourced fact is an invented fact until proven otherwise.

tests.name: Unresolved data conflicts
tests.measures: Kit flags that record two sources disagreeing (differs, website says, conflict, inconsistent, spells, both Group ...)
tests.computed: Regex over kit.json flags; minus conflicts the user resolved in confirm.json notes.
tests.why: Conflicting phone numbers, licences or names end up on a post.

tests.name: Ontario kits with a compliance line
tests.measures: Share of Ontario (and unknown-province, treated as Ontario) kits that have a complianceLine
tests.computed: kit.json province in (ON, null) and complianceLine non-empty.
tests.why: No line = proof-only = the piece can't be posted (O. Reg. 188/08).

tests.name: Assets awaiting confirmation
tests.measures: Assets marked 'check' that the user hasn't confirmed or rejected in the Desk
tests.computed: kit.json assets.check minus confirm.json assets decided true/false.
tests.why: Unconfirmed assets can't be used, so pieces fall back to weaker branding.

tests.name: Brand colours confirmed
tests.measures: Share of kits whose accent colour is confirmed (not provisional)
tests.computed: tokens.json color.accent $extensions.studio.provisional == false, or confirm.json colors.accent == true/#hex.
tests.why: Provisional colours are guesses from a website; wrong colours read as 'not our brand'.

tests.name: Accent colour usable on paper
tests.measures: Share of kits whose accent reaches 3:1 contrast against the paper colour
tests.computed: tokens.json color.accent $extensions.studio.contrastVsPaper >= 3.
tests.why: A low-contrast accent forces the director to improvise colours.

tests.name: Kits with a posting group
tests.measures: Share of kits with a group (drives batch and calendar)
tests.computed: kit.json group not null.
tests.why: No group = left out of weekly batches.

tests.name: Kit fact accuracy (spot-check)
tests.measures: Share of 5 sampled kit facts that match their cited source
tests.computed: Orchestrator picks 5 random (kit, filled key field) pairs, opens the provenance source (clients.json, footer image, website) and marks match / mismatch.
tests.why: Provenance says where a fact came from; this checks it was copied right.

tests.name: QA first-pass rate
tests.measures: Share of jobs whose first critic round passed
tests.computed: job.json log: first critic 'done: pass|...' vs 'done: fail|...'.
tests.why: Every extra round costs 10-100 minutes of director time and usage.

tests.name: Mean critic rounds to pass
tests.measures: Average number of critic rounds per job until pass
tests.computed: Count critic 'done:' lines per job (or qa/critique.json round).
tests.why: The trend line of how good first renders are.

tests.name: Critic rubric average
tests.measures: Mean of all scored rubric lines (1-5) in the final qa/critique.json of every job
tests.computed: critique.json scores; n/a and null skipped; per-line averages in detail.
tests.why: The single best summary of craft quality as judged by the critic.

tests.name: Weakest rubric line
tests.measures: The lowest per-line average across jobs (which line is dragging)
tests.computed: min over the 12 lines of mean(score).
tests.why: Shows the one skill to improve next (originality is usually it).

tests.name: Hard stops at Gate 2
tests.measures: Hard stops and coded QA fails still present when a piece reached Gate 2
tests.computed: critique.json hardStops (if present) + critique pass == false + qa/report.json pass == false, for jobs past the critic.
tests.why: A hard stop that reaches the owner is a process failure, not a taste issue.

tests.name: Near-dup distance to other clients
tests.measures: Smallest perceptual distance between a job's deliverables and any piece of a different client (library + other jobs)
tests.computed: pHash+dHash (64-bit), distance = mean Hamming; library/hashes.json (thumb + frames, client from cards) and other jobs' out/ (videos at 25/50/75%). QA fails at <= 6.
tests.why: Sibling clients must never get the same-looking post.

tests.name: Near-dup distance to competitors
tests.measures: Smallest perceptual distance between a job's deliverables and any Radar thumbnail
tests.computed: Same hashing against radar/thumbs/*.jpg (cached).
tests.why: We borrow mechanisms from competitors, never their look.

tests.name: Variety score
tests.measures: Mean variety.py novelty score of the chosen concepts
tests.computed: concepts.json chosen concept `novelty.score` (or the score parsed from the novelty text).
tests.why: Same style or device as last time = the feed looks templated.

tests.name: Compliance correctness
tests.measures: Share of Ontario (or unknown-province) pieces that carry the compliance line or are explicitly labelled PROOF
tests.computed: qa/report.json copy.compliance_line == pass, or check.json proofOnly, or 'PROOF' in the director/gate summary.
tests.why: A missing line on a postable Ontario piece is a regulatory breach.

tests.name: Maths verified
tests.measures: Share of numbers in check.json math that the checker recomputed as ok (jobs without check.json count as unverified)
tests.computed: check.json math[*].ok.
tests.why: One wrong payment figure costs a client's credibility.

tests.name: Postable without TODOs
tests.measures: Share of approved pieces that are not proof-only (could be posted today)
tests.computed: check.json proofOnly false and no 'PROOF' in the director summary.
tests.why: Approved-but-proof-only pieces are work the client never sees.

tests.name: QA waivers per piece
tests.measures: Mean number of coded-check waivers per job (qa/waivers.json)
tests.computed: len(waivers.json) per job.
tests.why: Waivers are fine once; a rising count means the gate or the engine needs fixing.

tests.name: Gate 1: picked without revision
tests.measures: Share of jobs whose first Gate 1 decision by the owner was a pick (not revise/reject)
tests.computed: library/feedback.jsonl g1 rows, first per job, excluding by == producer-test.
tests.why: The owner's own verdict on whether the concepts were good enough.

tests.name: Gate 2: approved without revision
tests.measures: Share of jobs whose first Gate 2 decision was approve with no fix request in the notes
tests.computed: library/feedback.jsonl g2 rows, first per job; notes asking for a fix (fix, wrong, not proper, change, redo, look into...) count as revision.
tests.why: The owner's verdict on the finished piece.

tests.name: Owner note themes
tests.measures: What the owner's gate notes are about (visual craft, copy, numbers, compliance, brand, pacing/sound)
tests.computed: Keyword themes over notes written at the Desk or in chat (producer test notes excluded). Informational.
tests.why: Tells you which agent to improve first.

tests.name: Critic agreement (spot-check)
tests.measures: Share of sampled critic line scores the orchestrator agrees with within 1 point
tests.computed: Orchestrator re-scores 6 random rubric lines on one recent job from full-size frames; agreement = |own - critic| <= 1.
tests.why: If the critic is lenient, every other creative number is inflated.

tests.name: Concepts genuinely different (spot-check)
tests.measures: Share of recent Gate 1 sets whose three concepts differ in device, structure and style
tests.computed: Orchestrator reads the last 3 concepts.json files and marks each set distinct / not distinct.
tests.why: Three versions of one idea is a fake choice.

tests.name: Approved pieces filed
tests.measures: Share of approved jobs that the librarian filed (library card exists or librarian node done)
tests.computed: library/cards/<job id>.json or index.jsonl card with source job + the job id, or job.json librarian done.
tests.why: Unfiled work is invisible to variety, near-dup and lessons, so the bot repeats itself.

tests.name: Client history updated
tests.measures: Share of approved jobs that appear in the client's kits/<slug>/history.json
tests.computed: history.json pieces[*].id/card matches the job id.
tests.why: variety.py reads history.json; a missing entry means the next piece can repeat the style.

tests.name: Gate decisions logged
tests.measures: Share of gate decisions in job.json that also appear in library/feedback.jsonl
tests.computed: (job, gate) pairs in job.json gates with a decision vs feedback.jsonl.
tests.why: Feedback is the only memory the strategist has of the owner's taste.

tests.name: Time: strategist
tests.measures: Median minutes the strategist worked per job (all its runs added up)
tests.computed: job.json log: 'strategist running' -> next 'strategist done|fail' segments, summed per job, median over jobs.
tests.why: Where the hours go; a slow stage is the first optimisation target.

tests.name: Time: checker
tests.measures: Median minutes the checker worked per job (all its runs added up)
tests.computed: job.json log: 'checker running' -> next 'checker done|fail' segments, summed per job, median over jobs.
tests.why: Where the hours go; a slow stage is the first optimisation target.

tests.name: Time: director
tests.measures: Median minutes the director worked per job (all its runs added up)
tests.computed: job.json log: 'director running' -> next 'director done|fail' segments, summed per job, median over jobs.
tests.why: Where the hours go; a slow stage is the first optimisation target.

tests.name: Time: critic
tests.measures: Median minutes the critic worked per job (all its runs added up)
tests.computed: job.json log: 'critic running' -> next 'critic done|fail' segments, summed per job, median over jobs.
tests.why: Where the hours go; a slow stage is the first optimisation target.

tests.name: Machine time per job
tests.measures: Median minutes of agent work per job, gate waits excluded
tests.computed: Sum of all node segments except gate waits.
tests.why: Total turnaround the owner waits on the bot.

tests.name: Owner time at gates
tests.measures: Median minutes jobs waited at Gate 1 + Gate 2
tests.computed: 'gate waiting' -> decision segments. Informational (owner time).
tests.why: Shows whether gates or agents are the bottleneck.

tests.name: Agent runs per job
tests.measures: Mean number of agent runs (strategist, checker, director, critic, librarian) per job
tests.computed: Count of 'running' log lines per job. The floor is 5 (concepts, script, check, render, critique).
tests.why: Each run costs usage; reruns mean something upstream was wrong.

tests.name: Failures in the last 30 days
tests.measures: Failed nodes, failed runner runs and error log lines
tests.computed: job.json nodes status failed + log lines starting fail/error (critic QA rounds excluded) + runner queue items failed/error.
tests.why: Failures that need a human to restart kill the 'one-line brief' promise.

tests.name: Restarts and usage waits
tests.measures: Runner retries (attempts > 1), runs that waited for a usage reset, and resumed runs
tests.computed: studio/runner/queue.json items.
tests.why: Restarts are the cost of running out of usage mid-job.

tests.name: Usage estimate (list price)
tests.measures: Sum of total_cost_usd and tokens reported by headless runs in the last 30 days
tests.computed: Result events in studio/runner/logs/*.jsonl and jobs/*/runs/*.jsonl. Chat-run jobs are not metered. Informational.
tests.why: Lets you see cost per job once production runs go through the runner.

tests.name: Briefs ready
tests.measures: Share of the 20 eval briefs whose readiness is 'ready' (fresh run_evals.py into a temp folder)
tests.computed: run_evals.py --out <tmp>; summary.ready / briefs.
tests.why: A brief that is proof-only or blocked at intake can't become a postable piece.

tests.name: Briefs with nothing to flag
tests.measures: Share of eval briefs with verdict pass (not warn/blocked)
tests.computed: summary.pass / briefs.
tests.why: Warnings are kit gaps the user can close.

tests.name: Briefs blocked
tests.measures: Eval briefs that cannot be produced as asked
tests.computed: summary.blocked.
tests.why: Blocked = the bot says no to a normal request.

tests.name: Golden concepts: rubric average
tests.measures: Mean critic-rubric score (concept-stage lines) of the best concept per golden brief
tests.computed: Latest studio/evals/golden/results/<YYYY-MM>.json, scored with golden_judge.md.
tests.why: Same 5 briefs every month = a clean trend line for the strategist's quality.

tests.name: Golden concepts: must-contain hits
tests.measures: Share of the golden briefs' must-contain items present in the chosen concept
tests.computed: Same results file, mustContain booleans.
tests.why: Checks the strategist follows the house rules and kit facts without being reminded.

tests.name: Golden concepts: hard stops
tests.measures: Hard stops found by the judge across the 5 golden briefs
tests.computed: Same results file, hardStops lists.
tests.why: A hard stop at concept stage would reach production.

tests.name: Days since the last golden run
tests.measures: Age of the latest golden results file
tests.computed: Today - results month/date.
tests.why: A monthly trend needs monthly runs.
